summary: Verified 2026-11-07 15:06-15:20, load 62-121, so timing is not_measured; no heavy harness was run. Rishal scores 7.0, below the reviewer's 7.2, and is NOT ON PAR (below 7.5, no blocker open). Build identity: rishal.glb and both skin GLBs are git-hash identical to ac10d5386^, so the GF-1 revert is confirmed. A numeric clip diff against the first-closing GLB (98b21f9b4, Oct 28) gives run, attack1, attack2, idle and idle_lobby at 0.0000 delta; recall was rebuilt (2 to 173 keys per channel); death changed; rest pose and vertex count (18,562) are identical. So the mesh, neck, strap and run/attack2 blade passes are exactly as the first closing review measured them. All three majors are confirmed. The base splash is a flatly lit model render pasted on the plate, and the Chalkline splash figure floats over the ledge. In all three portraits a brown striated 'wood' dowel neck (rishal.py:1348-1350, material 'wood' with folds displacement) sits under a smooth face plate, which pushes toward an artist's-mannequin read. There are still 27 joints and no cloth bones. Minors are kept. m5 is upgraded from 'not re-measured' to verified, because the clips are byte-for-byte equal in value. Score note: the base card every player sees still looks like an unpainted render, and the wood-dowel neck plus a faint face plate is the most-seen art, so 7.2 is slightly generous. Sensitivity: no blocker. The helm is a rounded segmented dome with a crescent crest, not a tall, pointed or conical hood, from the front (portrait), the back (backstrap_x2) and the gameplay camera (match_pair_x3). The face plate has brow, eye, nose and mouth ink lines and reads calm, not horror or hockey mask. The Lamplit face (warm beige, eye recess almost gone) over the wooden neck is the closest to the blank-mannequin line; m3 is kept as a watch item. Correction to the review: the vertex count is identical to the Oct 28 GLB, so the knife guards and grip wraps credited as 'now modelled' were already in the mesh at the first closing review. Credit them as verified present, not as new work.

findings.title: The base splash is a stiff, flatly lit model render pasted on the plate
findings.what: Static stance, one arm pointing a knife, flat ambient light. The tabard and chest are the brightest values, the face plate is small, the boots read as pale clumps, and there is no shared rim light from the plate. Correction: the figure is not small; it spans about y 90-810 of 900. The problem is staging and finish, not size. The Chalkline splash has its own dynamic pose, but its feet float above the ledge with no contact shadow.
findings.evidence: art/out/fighters/rishal/splash.png and rishal_chalkline_splash.png (viewed); the splash PNGs date from Nov 4, unchanged.
findings.gauge: A LoL base splash is a painted illustration with a narrative pose, a lit focal face or weapon, and a figure integrated with the scene's light.
findings.fix: As the reviewer proposed (a Glint Cut moment on the Aubade spires, the face as the value key, a warm rim from the plate's sun side, a paint-over pass), plus a contact shadow and grounding on the Chalkline card.
findings.verifierNote: Reproduced by viewing the card. Severity holds: this is the most-seen card and the weakest.

findings.title: A bare brown striated wooden dowel neck in every portrait; the brief's chalk gorget is missing
findings.what: The neck is deliberately built as a 'wood' part with fold displacement, which gives the vertical striation, and nothing covers it between the cowl and the face plate. Under a smooth pale face plate it reads as an artist's mannequin post on all three portraits.
findings.evidence: _harness/_shots/closing_rishal2v_faces_x3.png (base, lamplit and chalkline portraits cropped at 170,180-320,390, x3); art/blender/fighters/rishal.py:1348-1350 neck FlatCapsule with folds(0.0018, 60), material 'wood'; _design/fighters/rishal.md:61 and :77 name the chalk gorget; grep finds no gorget part in rishal.py.
findings.gauge: A LoL bust frames the face with a designed neck transition (collar, gorget or wrap).
findings.fix: Add the brief's chalk gorget: three overlapping carved lames rigid on the neck bone, about 150 tris. Repaint any visible neck in under-suit slate with no striation.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed in source and in all three portraits. This also feeds the mannequin-edge watch item.

findings.title: No secondary motion: 27 joints and no tabard, scarf or crest bones
findings.what: The skin joints are the core chains, x_visor_ridge and the knife tips only, and the brief's x_scarf is missing. Run, attack1 and attack2 are numerically identical to the Oct 28 GLB, so nothing new lags or settles.
findings.evidence: My GLB parse: skins[0].joints = 27 (root ... toe.R), materials body and accent; the Lamplit and Chalkline skins also have 27 joints. The clip diff against 98b21f9b4 gives a 0.0000 max delta on run, attack1, attack2 and idle. _design/fighters/rishal.md:62 names x_scarf.
findings.gauge: LoL cloth and trailing pieces lag 2-4 frames and settle after stops. This is a large part of an assassin's speed read.
findings.fix: Add front and back tabard flap bones and x_scarf, with baked lag and overshoot in run, dash, cast_a3 and cast_ult, and a settle on attack stops.

findings.title: At the gameplay camera the helm is a pale ovoid with prongs; the self accent is Noonwhite on a near-white helm
findings.what: As reported. Part of this is global: self = #F4EFE2 is a palette token for every fighter, and the self ring identifies the local player, so it stays minor.
findings.gauge: LoL heads are designed for the top-down camera with value breaks between helm, crest and face.
findings.fix: A mid-slate cap or nape plate under the crest; an ink keyline for the self accent on pale helms.

findings.title: The painted back X-strap has torn, speckled edges and grey smear
findings.evidence: _harness/_shots/closing_rishal2_backstrap_x2.png (viewed); the mesh and atlas are unchanged since the first closing review (GLB hash = ac10d5386^; vertex count 18,562 equals Oct 28).
findings.gauge: LoL strap and trim edges are clean at Collection zoom.
findings.fix: Paint the strap procedurally from its mask, with a lit top edge and an ink bottom edge.

findings.title: The face plate's eye recesses fade (worst on Lamplit), drifting toward a plain oval
findings.what: Base has a visible eye slit. On Lamplit the warm beige plate keeps only the brow, nose and mouth lines, and the eye is nearly gone. Together with M2's wood neck this is the closest the fighter comes to the blank-mannequin sensitivity line, but the carved lines keep it calm and not blank, so it is not a blocker.
findings.gauge: A LoL masked champion keeps a face read at every camera.
findings.fix: Inset the almond recesses 2-3 mm with ink at L* 20 or less; keep Lamplit's plate in cool chalk.
findings.verifierNote: This is a watch item: if M2 lands without fixing this, re-check the mannequin read.

findings.title: The crest is a single crescent frame, not the brief's two stacked plates
findings.gauge: A LoL model matches its published concept.
findings.fix: Add the second raked plate, or update the brief to the shipped crescent.

findings.title: The blade passes into the body in run and attack2
findings.what: The run and attack2 sampler outputs are numerically identical (0.0000 max delta) to the GLB the first closing review measured, and the rest pose and vertices are identical, so its measurement stands: run has 12 of 17 frames over 5 %, attack2 has 11 of 21.
findings.evidence: _harness/_reports/closing_rishal_blade_penetration.txt plus my clip diff (old GLB = git show 98b21f9b4:games/vale/art/out/fighters/rishal/rishal.glb).
findings.gauge: LoL keeps weapons clear of the body in gameplay clips.
findings.fix: Rotate the prop 10-15 deg outward in run and attack2.
findings.verifierNote: Upgraded from 'not re-measured' to verified by exact clip equality.
